description: A Birthing Pod chain interrupted by a counterspell on the key combo piece - proves the simulator does not falsely recognize a win when a combo line is legitimately disrupted, and continues correctly modeling legal actions afterward. Every spell/activation is paid from real printed costs against an explicitly tracked, paced land count (Birthing Pod's Phyrexian pip paid with life both times, matching the pitch/free-interaction category this deck also exercises via Force of Will in GBS-0012).
artificial_state_elements: Seat 2 is a synthetic generic opponent constructed specifically to hold up and cast a counterspell on cue - not a claim about real opponent play patterns.

Exact hand/land sequence hand-selected to reach the disruption point cleanly; land drops are paced one per seat-1 turn (turns 1/3/5/7/9) so every cost is paid from actually-untapped mana at the moment it happens.
material_characteristics: A countered spell never resolves - no permanent enters the battlefield and no enters-the-battlefield trigger occurs (CR 608.2b, CR 603.2)
Birthing Pod's search restriction (mana value exactly sacrificed value + 1) continues to apply correctly across multiple activations in the same game
Birthing Pod's own cast cost, {3}{G/P}, and its activation cost, {1}{G/P}, both carry a Phyrexian mana pip payable with 2 life instead of {G} (CR 118.10)
The game correctly continues (no winner) after the combo attempt fails - a disrupted line must not be silently treated as a win
abstracted_characteristics: Seat 2's hand/board beyond the one held-up counterspell and its own land drops
Exact identity of creatures found by Birthing Pod beyond their mana values

actions.action: Draw step: skipped (on the play, turn 1)

actions.notes: 2 lands untapped; holding both rather than casting anything this turn
3 lands untapped: Bayou, Savannah, Underground Sea

actions.action: Cast Birthing Pod, paying {3}{G/P} as 3 generic mana (all 3 lands) plus 2 life for the Phyrexian pip (20 -> 18)
actions.notes: CR 118.10 - Phyrexian mana may be paid with 2 life instead of the colored mana symbol

actions.action: Draw, play a land, pass, holding up mana
actions.notes: Constructed to represent an opponent holding a counterspell; 4 lands accumulated across turns 2/4/6

actions.action: Untap step: Bayou, Savannah, and Underground Sea untap

Activate Birthing Pod, paying {1}{G/P} as 1 generic mana plus 2 life (18 -> 16): sacrifice Delighted Halfling (mana value 1), search for a mana-value-2 creature (Devoted Druid), put it onto the battlefield
Draw, play a land, pass, holding up mana
Cast Hazel's Brewmaster, paying {3}{B}, intending to start the INT-0003 loop
actions.notes: Uses 4 of 5 untapped lands; 1 remains untapped. No Devoted Druid in graveyard yet this game - this specific cast wouldn't have a target for the exile trigger even if it resolved, but is cast anyway to demonstrate the counter interaction

actions.action: In response, cast a counterspell targeting Hazel's Brewmaster
actions.notes: Constructed disruption, paid from seat 2's own accumulated lands

actions.action: Hazel's Brewmaster is countered and put into seat 1's graveyard; its enters-the-battlefield trigger never happens because the spell never resolves and no permanent enters (CR 608.2b, CR 603.2)

Activate Birthing Pod again, paying {1}{G/P} as 1 generic mana (the last untapped land) plus 2 life (16 -> 14): sacrifice Devoted Druid (mana value 2), search for a mana-value-3 creature, put it onto the battlefield
actions.notes: Second Pod activation, independent of the first - no once-per-turn restriction on the ability itself beyond the permanent's own tap

actions.action: Pass turn with the combo unassembled and no attack declared

win_recognition_check: No state-based action for a win/loss condition is ever met in this sequence - Hazel's Brewmaster's countering prevents the INT-0003 loop from ever starting, both players remain above 0 life, and the simulator must correctly report the game as ongoing (not declare a winner) after the disruption.
rules_citations: CR 608.2b (countered spells go to the graveyard, never resolve)
CR 603.2 (triggered abilities require the triggering event to actually occur)
